chunks: And I found, in the handwriting of Saʿd ibn ʿAbdillāh, a hadith which he attributed to al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, that he said:

"Whoever has frequent forgetfulness in salat (prayer), let him say, when he enters the restroom: In the Name of Allah and by Allah; I seek refuge in Allah from the vile, impure, evil, defiling Shaytan, the accursed."

key_terms.أَعُوذُ بِاللَّهِ: I seek refuge in Allah, asking divine protection
key_terms.الرَّجِيمِ: the accursed one, driven away from mercy
key_terms.السَّهْوُ: forgetfulness or distraction, here in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الْخَلَاءَ: the place of relieving oneself, the restroom
key_terms.بِسْمِ اللَّهِ: In the Name of Allah, an opening formula of remembrance

ai.seo_question: What should a person say when entering the restroom if they frequently experience forgetfulness in salat (prayer)?
ai.summary: This hadith transmits a supplication to be recited upon entering the restroom for one who experiences frequent forgetfulness in salat (prayer). It connects seeking refuge in Allah with protection from the influence of the accursed Shaytan in a practical act of daily worship etiquette.
